newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Price data problems in NZ power mkt corrected - EMCO.
newsitem.headline: Price data problems in NZ power mkt corrected - EMCO.

text.p: The Electricity Market Company (EMCO) of New Zealand on Thursday said it had corrected data inconsistencies which had pushed some wholesale electricity prices above 20 cents per kilowatt hour in the past few days.
"These price 'spikes' will not appear in final prices published at the end of the month and consumers should not be affected, EMCO chief executive Lincoln Gould said in a statement.
He said none of the problems indicated that there was a fundamental design or systems flaw.
"They have occurred as a result of several factors that relate to the information flows to the computers and not problems with the computers themselves."

However, not all the high provisional prices had been caused by data inconsistencies. EMCO was analysing the problems that had led to sharply higher North Island prices for Tuesday and Wednesday of this week.

These spikes appeared to have stemmed from several factors including under-bidding for electricity by power companies and traders, limitations on power transfers across the Cook Strait cable and limited availability of generation in the North

"All these factors mean there have been mismatches between the information supplied to the market in advance and what actually happened in specific half hours for which electricity was priced," Gould said.
"Steps have been taken to ensure that these information mismatches do not continue."
